blocks.text: Within the Zscaler Admin Console, you can add up to 500 links per user portal. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations.
To add links to a user portal:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Browser > Web Access > Portal Links.
Click Add.

blocks.text: The Add Portal Links page appears.

blocks.item: On the Add Portal Links page:
App Type
On the App Type tab:
Private Applications: Select if links in the user portal point to private applications configured in Private Access (ZPA).
Public Applications: Select if links in the user portal point to public applications that are accessible to users but not configured in Private Access.
Click Next.
See image.
Link Type
On the Link Type tab:
If you selected Private Applications in the previous step:

User Portal: Select the user portal that can display these links. You can search for a user portal, click Select All Displayed, click the Delete icon next to the selection to remove it, or click Clear All to remove all selections.

Application Segments: Select the application segments you want to associate to the user portals from the drop-down menu. The links you specify are based on the applications included in these segments. You can search for an application segment, click Select All Displayed, click the Delete icon next to the selection to remove it, or click Clear All to remove all selections.

Applications: Select the applications that you want to include within the application segments you selected previously. Click Clear All to remove all selections. The application segment name and application segment domain both appear in the drop-down menu.
See image.
If you selected Public Applications in the previous step:

User Portal: Select the user portal that can display these links. You can select more than one user portal. You can search for a user portal, click Select All Displayed, click the Delete icon next to a selection to remove it, or click Clear All to remove all selections.
Under URLs:
Select a protocol for the link (i.e., HTTP or HTTPS).
Enter a fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the application (e.g., www.example.com).
(Optional) Enter a specific path for the URL (e.g., entering /preferences creates a link pointing to www.example.com/preferences).
(Optional) Click Add to add more public URLs.
See image.
Click Next.

During configuration, you can only add up to 150 links at a time. For a complete list of ranges and limits per feature, see Ranges & Limitations. To avoid incorrect or inconsistent policy evaluation, a private application should not be used to a create a Public Applications link type. Zscaler recommends the following when adding a Public Applications link to an application segment:
Delete the public applications user portal link.
Enter the application when configuring an application segment.
Create the private applications user portal link with the application configured in the application segment.
On the Links page, a links list for all of the selected applications is displayed. Click Expand All to see more information about each link. Configure the following link information, as needed:
Name: The name of the link and how it appears in the user portal.

If you selected Private Applications in the App Type step, the link name as specified in the application segment is displayed by default. To change this name, click the link and enter the new name in the Name field. For example, if the default name is www.example.com, you can change it to My Example Application.
If you selected Public Applications in the App Type step, the link name you entered in the Link Type step is displayed.
Display on Portal: Select Enabled to display the link in the user portal. If Disabled is selected, the link is not displayed on the user portal.
Protocol: Select a protocol for the link.
If you selected Private Applications in the App Type step:
For private applications where Browser Access is not enabled, you can specify HTTP or HTTPS.
For private applications where Browser Access is enabled, this field defaults to the protocol that was configured in the application segment, and it cannot be changed.
If you selected Public Applications in the App Type step, you must specify HTTP or HTTPS. By default, this field is populated based on the protocol selection.
Domain: The domain name used in the URL for the link.

If you selected Private Applications in the App Type step, the domain as specified in the application segment is displayed by default. To change this name, click the link and enter the new domain in the Domain field.
If this is a Browser Access-enabled application, the FQDN as specified in the application segment is displayed by default.
If this is an application that can only be accessed with Zscaler Client Connector, the IP address or FQDN as specified in the application segment is displayed by default.
Regardless of whether the application is Browser Access-enabled or requires Zscaler Client Connector, the URL string supports HTTP and HTTPS protocols.
If you selected Public Applications in the App Type step, the domain you entered in the Link Type step is displayed.

Path: (Optional) By default this is set to forward slash (/), but you can edit this field to use a specific path for the URL. For example, an HTTPS link to www.exampleapp1.com would have a URL of https://www.exampleapp1.com/ by default. However, you can change the path to /preferences so that the URL points to https://www.exampleapp1.com/preferences.
Description: (Optional) Enter a description for the link.
Logo/Favicon: (Optional) Click Select Image to upload a logo or favicon for the link. You can upload any valid .ico, .jpg, or .png image file type that is 32x32 pixels or smaller.
Click Next.
See image.

If a user is connecting to Private Access via Zscaler Client Connector on at least one device, they see links for applications they can access across all devices. However, an access policy restricts access to an application based on the Zscaler Client Connector Posture Profile criteria.

For example, you can have an access policy rule that allows a user to access the HR application on their Windows device, but have another rule that allows them to access the sales application on their macOS device. In this example, the user sees links for the HR application and sales application on the user portal, but they can only access an application if they are using the proper device. To learn more, see About Access Policy and About Device Posture Profiles.
